facts.content: Patient has 4 to 5 bowel movements per day which are watery or loose.
Patient had one episode of vomiting.
There is no blood or mucus in the stool.
Patient possibly has a low-grade fever and decreased appetite but is maintaining oral fluid intake.
facts.source_text: Possible low-grade fever; ↓ appetite; maintaining PO fluids

facts.content: There has been no recent travel or suspicious food consumption.
facts.source_text: No recent travel; no suspicious foods

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses an inhaler named 'Laxepro' which is yellow.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer about 10 years ago at age 62.
facts.source_text: Father—HTN; died of bowel CA at 62 (~10 yrs ago)

facts.content: Video impression shows no signs of dehydration.
facts.source_text: Video impression: no signs of dehydration

facts.content: Acute diarrhea for 3 days with mild crampy abdominal pain, single emesis, 4 to 5 bowel movements per day, no blood or mucus; patient is tolerating fluids and has no travel or food exposures.
facts.source_text: Acute diarrhea x3 days with mild crampy abd pain and single emesis; 4–5/day; no blood/mucus; tolerating fluids; no travel/food exposures

facts.content: Encourage fluid intake and use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte OTC).
Recommend soft foods like crackers, toast, jam, boiled vegetables, and mashed potatoes; avoid milk, meat, eggs, and fish during active diarrhea; yogurt and probiotics are acceptable.
facts.source_text: Diet: soft foods (e.g., crackers, toast, jam); boiled veg/mash; avoid milk; avoid meat/eggs/fish during active diarrhea; yoghurt/probiotics OK

facts.content: Reintroduce meat, eggs, and fish after 48 hours symptom-free.
Provide safety net advice for symptoms persisting more than one week, blood in the stool, increased stool frequency to 6 to 8 per day, or signs of dehydration.
facts.source_text: Safety net: If persists >1 week or any blood in stool → send stool sample (may need abx depending on results); If stool freq increases to ≥6–8/day or signs of dehydration → seek urgent care/hospital

facts.content: Instruct patient to contact the service if symptoms worsen or for any concerns.
Patient advised that instructions are available in the app for review.
facts.source_text: Patient advised instructions available in app for review
